thread:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH_QUEUE_DEPTH for /v1/generate in prod-us-east-1. Incident INC-2026-93 triggered. Notify @oncall-eng.

jordan: Acknowledged. Seeing queue depth ~330, tail latency spiking >6s. Paging.

sam: Confirming GPU pool 'pool-gpu-a' at 92% and pod creation stalled. HPA logs show backoff due to warmup_in_progress.

maya: Support update: ~20 customers reporting slow responses/timeouts, some 120s client timeouts. Marking P1 customer impact.

liam: Initial read: we rotated model artifacts at 03:09 UTC which bumped image pulls. Registry latency spiked around that time.

anika: Can we flip routes to a smaller model variant for low-latency routes? model:v1.3-lite exists.

jordan: Proceed with fallback. Apply route override to /v1/generate -> model:v1.3-lite, canary -> full.

opsbot: Route override applied in prod-us-east-1: /v1/generate -> model:v1.3-lite (100%).

sam: Kube events show image pull timeout errors and repeated warmup failures:
```
[03:10:21] kube: Failed to pull image: context deadline exceeded
[03:10:24] autoscaler: warmup_in_progress=6, deny_scale=true
[03:10:30] runtime: queue_depth=342, p99=6200ms
```

liam: Also seeing prefix cache cold-start after rotation; cache misses spiked ~18%. That amplifies latency.

anika: I'm increasing HPA minReplicas 2->7 for pool-gpu-a to get capacity in asap. Command executed.

sam: Pods are launching but image pulls still slow due to registry throughput issue. I'll enable overflow to prod-us-west-1 region.

opsbot: Overflow routing enabled: pool-gpu-a overflow -> prod-us-west-1. Batching max_size reduced to 6 to lower tail latency.

maya: After routing + model fallback, customer error rate dropped from 7% to 1.5% within 8 minutes. Not fully resolved but mitigated.

jordan: Collecting artifacts for RCA. Please upload autoscaler logs, kube events, runtime traces for 03:05-03:25 UTC.

sam: Uploaded: s3://redwood-incident-logs/INC-2026-93/log_bundle_2365.tar.gz

anika: Hypotheses to track in post-incident thread:
- H1: Registry image-pull latency during model rotations caused pod warmup to stall -> HPA unable to scale fast enough.
- H2: warmup_in_progress throttle overly conservative for sudden churn.
- H3: routing cooldown prevented immediate cross-region overflow earlier.

liam: Reproduction plan: in staging, simulate slow registry by delaying image pulls and trigger model rotation; measure queue growth, HPA behavior, and cache miss penalty.

maya: Support to customer comms: sending updates that we routed traffic, applied smaller model fallback, and scaling changes; will follow up with timeline and postmortem.

jordan: Night oncall handoff in 20m. Leaving runbook: if registry still degraded, revert canary and keep overflow enabled until registry healthy; reset HPA minReplicas to policy after recovery.

sam: Temporary remediations applied: route fallback, forced HPA scale-up, overflow region, reduced batching. Leaving checklist in incident doc.

opsbot: Incident INC-2026-93 status: mitigated -> monitoring at 03:25 UTC. Pager cleared.

anika: Owners for postmortem: sam (infra), liam (runtime), anika (deploy). Expect draft in 48h. I'll add tests for warmup throttle behavior and canary rotation procedure.

liam: I'll instrument image-pull latency and prefix-cache-miss metrics per rotation, add alert if image-pull >5s or cache-miss >15%.

maya: Noting impacted customers list updated in incident doc and support ladder engaged for follow-ups.

jordan: TL;DR for handoff: registry pull slowness during model rotation caused warmup stalls -> HPA backoff -> queue spike. Mitigations: route to lite model, HPA bump, overflow to another region, reduce batch size. Postmortem to validate warmup throttling heuristics and add safer rotation canary.

opsbot: Handoff posted to #incidents: INC-2026-93. Link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-93
